metadata.title: islam.museum: A Citable Open Knowledge Graph and Digital Museum of Islamic History — Resource Description, Method and Validation State
metadata.description: Open, reusable and citable structured data on Islamic history remain scarce in comparison with the size of the written tradition. Institutional collection portals are authoritative but are generally not designed for bulk reuse, while large content sites are rarely structured or cited at the level of the individual claim. This paper describes islam.museum, an Arabic-first digital museum, with English and Urdu editions, whose primary form is a knowledge graph kept in a public git repository and archived on Zenodo under the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23692511. On the repository basis analysed here (commit 63475724ce, 15 November 2026) the resource holds 64,374 record files: 54,823 content records and 9,551 source records, connected by 88,506 typed relations. Data are released under CC0 1.0, prose under CC BY-SA 4.0 and code under the MIT licence; media are licensed per item. The resource is compiled by one person directing AI tools under written rules: the tools research, draft, translate and check records, and automated gates validate schema, citations, encoding and content-safety rules before anything is merged. The validation state is reported without adjustment. 81.1% of content records are drafts; 55.1% cite at least one book; 20.5% are preliminary cards imported from Wikidata whose sources are not yet checked. All records are AI-written unless a record itself shows otherwise, and the corpus is not human-reviewed. No claim-level accuracy audit has yet been completed; a protocol for one is specified. The project was launched on 11 October 2026, has had no formal user study, and no independent citations of the dataset were known at the time of writing. The resource may be reused as a dataset, queried through a static JSON API, mapped to school curricula, or forked as a template for other heritage domains.
metadata.notes: AI-use disclosure: AI tools assisted with research, drafting, translation and checking under the author's direction; the author is solely responsible for the claims. Cite the dataset by its concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23692511; the version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24246204 (v2026.11.15) only pins the analysed snapshot.

_notes_for_the_author_remove_before_uplo.paper_doi: 10.5281/zenodo.24273663 - Zenodo assigns it; reserve it in the upload form first so it can be printed in the PDF.
_notes_for_the_author_remove_before_uplo.licence_choice: CC BY 4.0 is recommended for the paper text: it is the licence most data and methods journals use, so a later journal version does not conflict with the preprint, and it lets indexers and readers redistribute the PDF. It applies to this paper only. It does not change the dataset's split: data CC0 1.0, prose CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT, media per item.
_notes_for_the_author_remove_before_uplo.relation_choice: The dataset concept DOI is related twice. 'cites' is the relation that DataCite and the aggregators built on it count as a citation of the dataset, which is the purpose of this paper. 'describes' states what kind of paper this is (a data paper). 'isSupplementedBy' was considered and not used for the dataset: it says the dataset is a supplement to the paper, whereas here the paper exists to describe the dataset. If Zenodo's form rejects two relations to one identifier, keep 'cites'.
_notes_for_the_author_remove_before_uplo.reciprocal_link: After deposit, edit the DATASET record to add this paper's DOI with relation 'isDescribedBy' (and 'isCitedBy'). This creates a new dataset version only if files change; a metadata-only edit does not.
_notes_for_the_author_remove_before_uplo.field_names: Written for Zenodo's deposit API metadata format (as used by .zenodo.json). If the web form is used instead, enter the same values by hand.
